learn.hook: 3 kurtas and 4 pairs of jeans: how many outfits? You don't need to list them — 3 × 4 = 12. That multiplication is the most powerful idea in counting.
points: Counting by listing is slow and error-prone; the counting principles let us count arrangements and selections without listing.
Multiplication principle: if one event can happen in m ways and, after it, another can happen in n ways, the two together can happen in m × n ways.
It extends to any number of events: m × n × p × … ways.
Use it for building codes, numbers, number plates and signals position by position: fill each place in turn and multiply the choices.
Example: signals made by hoisting 2 of 4 different flags one below the other: 4 × 3 = 12 signals.

example.q: How many 3-digit numbers can be formed from the digits 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 if no digit is repeated?

learn.reallife: An Indian vehicle number like MH 12 AB 1234 is built position by position; the multiplication principle tells the RTO how many plates a series can issue.

items.q: 2 routes A→B, 4 routes B→C: routes A→C via B
4 flags, signals using 2 flags one below the other

games.title: Counting principle check
items: If a task has two stages with 5 and 6 ways, there are 30 ways in all.
Tossing a coin 4 times gives 8 outcomes.
The multiplication principle works for more than two events.
Multiply the number of ways for each stage.
Choosing 1 of 3 pens AND 1 of 4 pencils gives 7 ways.
Signals with 3 of 5 different flags one below another: 60.

quiz.q: A restaurant thali offers 4 choices of dal, 3 of sabzi and 2 of dessert. How many different thalis are possible?
quiz.explain: 4 × 3 × 2 = 24 by the multiplication principle.
quiz.mistake: Adds the choices instead of multiplying

quiz.q: How many outcomes are there when a coin is tossed 5 times?
quiz.explain: Each toss has 2 outcomes: 2⁵ = 32.

quiz.q: How many 2-digit even numbers can be formed from the digits 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 if digits may be repeated?
quiz.explain: Units digit must be 2 or 4 (2 ways); tens digit any of 5. 2 × 5 = 10.
quiz.mistake: Ignores the even condition and gives 25

quiz.q: A signal uses 3 of 6 different flags hoisted one below the other. How many signals are possible?
quiz.explain: 6 × 5 × 4 = 120 (a flag cannot be used twice).
quiz.mistake: Uses 6³, allowing the same flag twice

quiz.q: How many 3-digit numbers have all their digits from 1 to 9 and no digit repeated?

From city A to B there are 3 trains, and from B to C there are 5 buses. In how many ways can Meera go from A to C via B and return to A via B, using a different train and a different bus on the way back?
quiz.explain: Going: 3 × 5 = 15. Returning with different ones: 4 × 2 = 8. Total 15 × 8 = 120.
quiz.mistake: Allows the same train and bus on the return

quiz.q: An exam has 6 true/false questions. In how many ways can a student answer all of them?
quiz.explain: 2 choices for each of 6 questions: 2⁶ = 64.

quiz.q: Why do we multiply, not add, the number of ways in the counting principle?
options: Because tasks happen at the same time
Because adding is only for permutations
Because multiplication gives a bigger number
Each way of doing the first task can be combined with every way of doing the second
quiz.explain: For each of the m choices there are n follow-ups, giving m groups of n, i.e. m × n.

teach.ask: Gappu has 3 caps and 4 scarves and wants to know how many combos he can wear. Explain the fundamental principle of counting.
teach.praise: For every cap, 4 scarves: 3 × 4 = 12 looks. I'm the best-dressed bird in the sky!
teach.nudge: Why do we multiply 3 by 4 and not add them?

learn.hook: A 4-digit UPI PIN can repeat digits; a lucky-draw ticket with all-different digits cannot. That one rule changes the count completely.
points: With repetition allowed, every position has the full number of choices: 4-digit PINs from 0–9 = 10⁴ = 10,000.
Without repetition, the choices drop by one at each step: 10 × 9 × 8 × 7 = 5040.
Fill restricted positions FIRST (e.g. the units digit for even numbers, the first digit that cannot be 0).
Words from letters: 'word' means any arrangement of letters, with or without meaning.
Example: 4-letter codes from the first 10 letters of the alphabet without repetition: 10 × 9 × 8 × 7 = 5040.

example.q: How many 4-digit even numbers can be formed from the digits 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 without repetition?
steps: Units digit: 2 or 4 → 2 choices (fill it first).

learn.reallife: Mobile numbers in India have 10 digits starting with 6, 7, 8 or 9 — counting with repetition explains why TRAI never runs out quickly.

games.title: Repetition allowed or not?
items: Answer key of an MCQ test

items.q: 4-letter words from A, B, C, D, E, repetition allowed

quiz.q: How many 3-digit numbers can be formed from the digits 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 with no digit repeated?
quiz.explain: First digit cannot be 0: 4 choices; then 4 remaining for tens (including 0) and 3 for units. 4 × 4 × 3 = 48.

quiz.q: How many 4-letter codes can be made from the first 8 letters of the English alphabet without repetition?
6-digit phone numbers in a town all begin with 98 and use the digits 0–9 with no digit repeated. How many such numbers are possible?
quiz.explain: After 9 and 8, 8 digits remain for 4 places: 8 × 7 × 6 × 5 = 1680.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that 9 and 8 are already used

quiz.q: How many 3-digit odd numbers can be formed using 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 if repetition is allowed?
quiz.explain: Units digit odd: 1, 3, 5 (3 ways); hundreds and tens: 6 each. 3 × 6 × 6 = 108.

quiz.q: How many 5-letter 'words' (with or without meaning) can be formed from the letters of DELHI with no letter repeated?
In how many ways can 3 different prizes be given to 5 students if a student may win more than one prize?
quiz.explain: Each prize can go to any of 5 students: 5³ = 125.
quiz.mistake: Uses 5 × 4 × 3, assuming no student wins twice

quiz.q: How many numbers between 100 and 1000 can be formed using 1, 3, 5, 7 if repetition is allowed?
quiz.explain: Such numbers have 3 digits, each from 4 choices: 4³ = 64.

quiz.q: To count 3-digit even numbers from 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 without repetition, which place should be filled first?
options: It does not matter at all
quiz.explain: The units place carries the restriction (must be 2 or 4); filling it first avoids double counting.
quiz.mistake: Fills the restricted place last and over-counts

teach.ask: Gappu doesn't know why 4-digit PINs are 10,000 but 4-digit codes with different digits are only 5040. Explain the difference.
teach.praise: With repetition every place has 10 choices; without it, the choices shrink. Mystery solved!
teach.nudge: What happens to the number of choices for the next place when digits cannot repeat?

learn.hook: In how many ways can 11 players walk out in a line before a World Cup match? 11! = 39,916,800. Factorials grow FAST.
points: A permutation is an arrangement of objects in a definite order.
Number of permutations of n different objects taken r at a time (no repetition): nPr = n(n − 1)(n − 2)…(n − r + 1) = n!/(n − r)!, 0 ≤ r ≤ n.
Derivation: fill r places one by one — n choices, then n − 1, …, then n − r + 1 — and multiply.
With repetition allowed, the number of arrangements of n objects taken r at a time is nʳ.
learn.reallife: The BCCI's selection panel ranking 3 players for 'captain, vice-captain, wicketkeeper' from 15 is ¹⁵P₃ = 2730 ordered choices.

games.title: Derive nPr = n!/(n − r)!
items: First place can be filled in n ways
Second place in (n − 1) ways, …, r-th place in (n − r + 1) ways

quiz.q: Evaluate ⁷P₃.
What is the value of 0! + 1!?
quiz.explain: 0! = 1 by definition and 1! = 1, so the sum is 2.
3! + 4! = 6 + 24 = 30, while 7! = 5040. Factorials do not add like this.

quiz.q: In how many ways can 4 different books be arranged on a shelf from a collection of 9 different books?

quiz.mistake: Keeps only one of the terms

quiz.q: How many 3-letter codes can be made from 26 letters if repetition is allowed?
The value of n!/(n − 2)! is:
Evaluate n!/(r!(n − r)!) for n = 6, r = 2.
quiz.mistake: Forgets r! in the denominator, getting 30

teach.ask: Gappu thinks 0! should be 0 and that 3! + 4! = 7!. Explain factorials and the formula for nPr.
teach.praise: 0! is 1, factorials don't add, and nPr = n!/(n − r)!. My counting is sharper now!
teach.nudge: What is 0! defined to be, and why?

learn.hook: Swap the two Os in 'BALLOON' and nothing changes. That's why arrangements of alike letters need dividing, not just multiplying.
points: If p of n objects are alike (and the rest different), the number of arrangements of all n is n!/p!.
Reason: swapping the p alike objects among themselves (p! ways) gives the same arrangement, so n! counts each one p! times.
If p₁, p₂, …, pₖ objects are alike of k kinds, the number of arrangements is n!/(p₁! p₂! … pₖ!).
Example: MISSISSIPPI has 11 letters with I × 4, S × 4, P × 2: 11!/(4! 4! 2!) = 34,650.
ALLAHABAD has 9 letters with A × 4, L × 2: 9!/(4! 2!) = 7560.

example.q: How many different words can be formed from the letters of BALLOON?
steps: 7 letters: B, A, L, L, O, O, N.
L appears 2 times, O appears 2 times.

learn.reallife: A DNA sequence of 10 bases with 4 A, 3 G, 2 C and 1 T can be arranged in 10!/(4! 3! 2! 1!) = 12,600 ways — biotech labs count exactly like this.

items.text: Arrangements of n objects, p alike = n!/___

quiz.q: How many distinct arrangements of the letters of BANANA are there?
How many different words can be made from the letters of COMMITTEE?
quiz.mistake: Divides by only one or two of the 2!s

quiz.q: In how many ways can 3 red, 2 blue and 1 green ball (balls of the same colour identical) be arranged in a row?
How many arrangements of the letters of ALLAHABAD are there?
quiz.explain: 9 letters: A × 4, L × 2, others single. 9!/(4! 2!) = 7560.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to divide by 2! for the Ls

quiz.q: Why do we divide by p! when p objects are alike?
options: Because permuting the alike objects among themselves gives no new arrangement
Because alike objects cannot be arranged
quiz.explain: Each distinct arrangement is counted p! times in n!, once for each order of the alike objects.
quiz.mistake: Thinks alike objects are simply removed

quiz.q: How many 4-digit numbers can be formed using the digits 1, 1, 2, 2 (each used once)?
quiz.mistake: Treats the repeated digits as different

quiz.q: How many distinct words can be made with the letters of MISSISSIPPI?
quiz.mistake: Forgets the 2! for the two Ps

quiz.q: The letters of LEVEL are arranged in all possible ways. How many arrangements are there?

teach.ask: Gappu counts the words from BANANA as 720. Explain why that is too many and how to correct it.
teach.praise: Swapping the As doesn't make a new word, so divide by 3! and 2!. Only 60 words!
teach.nudge: If you swap two As in BANANA, do you get a new word?

learn.hook: 'Vowels must sit together', 'the number must be divisible by 5' — exam questions love conditions. The trick: handle the condition first.
points: Vowels together: glue them into one block, arrange the block with the other letters, then arrange the vowels inside the block.
Vowels never together = (all arrangements) − (arrangements with all vowels together), when the condition is 'not all together'.
Fixed positions: if a word must start or end with given letters, place them first, then arrange the rest.
Divisibility: even → last digit even; divisible by 5 → last digit 0 or 5; divisible by 10 → last digit 0. Fill that place first.
To find n from a relation like nP5 = 20 nP3, write both sides as products and cancel: (n − 3)(n − 4) = 20, so n = 8.

example.q: In how many arrangements of the letters of DAUGHTER are the vowels together? In how many are they not all together?
steps: DAUGHTER has 8 different letters; vowels A, U, E.
Glue the vowels: 5 consonants + 1 block = 6 units → 6! = 720.

learn.reallife: Seating plans at a wedding ('keep the family of the bride together') are vowels-together problems in disguise.

games.title: Arrangements of MONDAY starting with M and ending with Y
items: Fix M in the first place and Y in the last place
Letters left for the middle: O, N, D, A

items.q: Words from MONDAY starting with M
Words from 4 different letters, a given letter first
4-digit numbers from 1–5, no repetition, divisible by 5
Arrange 3 boys and 2 girls in a row, girls together

quiz.q: Find n if ⁿP₄ = 12 × ⁿP₂.
Find n if ⁿP₅ = 20 × ⁿP₃.
How many 4-digit numbers divisible by 10 can be formed from 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 without repetition?
quiz.explain: Units digit must be 0. The other 3 places come from 5 digits: 5 × 4 × 3 = 60.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to fix the last digit as 0

quiz.q: In how many arrangements of the letters of EQUATION do all the vowels occur together?
quiz.explain: Vowels E, U, A, I, O form one block; with Q, T, N that is 4 units → 4! = 24. Inside the block 5! = 120. Total 24 × 120 = 2880.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to arrange the vowels within the block

quiz.q: In how many arrangements of DAUGHTER are the vowels NOT all together?
quiz.explain: Total 8! = 40320 minus together 6! × 3! = 4320 gives 36,000.

quiz.q: How many 3-digit even numbers can be formed from 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7 with no repetition?
quiz.explain: Units digit from 2, 4, 6 (3 ways); then 5 and 4 for the other places: 3 × 5 × 4 = 60.

quiz.q: How many words can be made from the letters of MONDAY using all letters, if the word must start with a vowel?
quiz.explain: Vowels are O and A (2 choices for the first place); the remaining 5 letters: 5! = 120. 2 × 120 = 240.

quiz.q: In how many ways can 4 boys and 3 girls stand in a row if the girls occupy the even places (2nd, 4th, 6th)?
quiz.explain: Girls in the 3 even places: 3! = 6; boys in the 4 odd places: 4! = 24. 6 × 24 = 144.
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of multiplies, or ignores the condition

teach.ask: Gappu wants the number of arrangements of DAUGHTER with vowels together. Explain the 'glue the block' trick and how to get 'not together'.
teach.praise: Glue, arrange, unglue — and subtract for 'not together'. That's a neat trick!
teach.nudge: After gluing the vowels into a block, what else must you multiply by?

learn.hook: Choosing 3 friends for a trip to Goa is a combination — the order you pick them doesn't matter. Ranking them 1st, 2nd, 3rd would be a permutation.
points: A combination is a selection where order does not matter.
nCr = n!/(r!(n − r)!), 0 ≤ r ≤ n. Each selection of r objects can be arranged in r! ways, so nPr = r! × nCr.
nC0 = nCn = 1, and nCr = nC(n − r) (choosing r to take = choosing n − r to leave).
If nCa = nCb, then a = b or a + b = n.
Pascal's rule: nCr + nC(r − 1) = (n + 1)Cr.
learn.reallife: A cricket selector picking 15 players from 25 probables for a squad is choosing a combination: ²⁵C₁₅ = 3,268,760 squads are possible.

games.title: Permutation or combination?
items: Choosing 3 books to take on a trip
Electing a president and a secretary

quiz.q: Evaluate ¹⁰C₃.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to divide by 3!, giving ¹⁰P₃ = 720

quiz.q: If ⁿC₂ = 45, then n is:
If ⁿC₁₀ = ⁿC₆, then ⁿC₂ is:
Using Pascal's rule, ⁸C₅ + ⁸C₄ equals:
quiz.explain: nCr + nC(r − 1) = (n + 1)Cr with n = 8, r = 5 gives ⁹C₅.
quiz.mistake: Adds the upper and lower numbers

quiz.q: If ⁿP_r = 720 and ⁿC_r = 120, then r is:
Which is equal to ²⁰C₁₇?
quiz.explain: nCr = nC(n − r): ²⁰C₁₇ = ²⁰C₃.

quiz.q: In how many ways can a committee of 3 be chosen from 9 people?
quiz.explain: ⁹C₃ = (9 × 8 × 7)/6 = 84. Order does not matter in a committee.

quiz.q: If ²ⁿC₃ : ⁿC₃ = 11 : 1, then n is:

teach.ask: Gappu thinks choosing 3 friends and ranking 3 friends give the same count. Explain combinations, nCr and how it links to nPr.
teach.praise: Selecting ignores order, so divide the permutations by r!. Team picking made easy!
teach.nudge: If order does not matter, why do we divide nPr by r!?

learn.hook: The school quiz team needs 2 boys and 3 girls, with at least one Class 12 student. Questions like this mix combinations with 'at least' and 'at most'.
points: Separate groups: choose from each group and multiply, e.g. 2 boys from 7 and 3 girls from 5: ⁷C₂ × ⁵C₃.
'At least' / 'at most': add the cases, or use total − unwanted cases (e.g. at least 1 girl = total − no girls).
Cards: a deck has 52 cards, 4 suits of 13, 4 aces, 12 face cards (J, Q, K). Exactly one ace in 4 cards: ⁴C₁ × ⁴⁸C₃.
Lines through n points (no three collinear): ⁿC₂. Triangles: ⁿC₃. Diagonals of an n-gon: ⁿC₂ − n.
Read 'exactly', 'at least' and 'at most' carefully — they decide which cases to add.

example.q: A committee of 5 is to be formed from 6 boys and 5 girls with exactly 3 boys and 2 girls. In how many ways?

learn.reallife: A Ranji Trophy squad selection ('at least 4 bowlers, at most 2 wicket-keepers') is solved with exactly these case-by-case combinations.

games.title: At least 1 girl in a team of 3 from 5 boys and 4 girls
items: Use the complement: at least 1 girl = total − teams with no girl
Subtract the no-girl teams (⁵C₃ = 10) from this total

quiz.q: In how many ways can a team of 3 boys and 2 girls be chosen from 7 boys and 5 girls?
From 5 boys and 4 girls, how many teams of 3 have at least one girl?
quiz.explain: Total ⁹C₃ = 84; teams with no girls ⁵C₃ = 10. 84 − 10 = 74.
quiz.mistake: Counts only teams with exactly one girl

quiz.q: In how many ways can 4 cards be drawn from a deck of 52 so that exactly one is an ace?
quiz.explain: Choose the ace: ⁴C₁ = 4. Choose 3 non-aces from 48: ⁴⁸C₃ = 17,296. 4 × 17,296 = 69,184.

quiz.q: In how many ways can 4 cards of the same suit be chosen from a deck?
quiz.explain: Choose the suit (4 ways) and 4 of its 13 cards: 4 × ¹³C₄ = 4 × 715 = 2860.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to multiply by the 4 suits

quiz.q: How many triangles can be formed using 12 points in a plane, no three of which are collinear?
How many diagonals does an octagon have?
quiz.explain: ⁸C₂ − 8 = 28 − 8 = 20 (remove the 8 sides).

quiz.q: A student must answer 7 of 10 questions, choosing at least 3 from the first 5. In how many ways can she choose? (She can take 3, 4 or 5 from the first group.)
quiz.explain: 3 from first: ⁵C₃ × ⁵C₄ = 50; 4: ⁵C₄ × ⁵C₃ = 50; 5: ⁵C₅ × ⁵C₂ = 10. Total 110.
quiz.mistake: Misses the case of all 5 from the first group

quiz.q: In how many ways can a hand of 4 cards be all face cards?
quiz.explain: There are 12 face cards; ¹²C₄ = 495.

teach.ask: Gappu must pick a team with 'at least one girl' and is counting case by case. Show a faster way and explain how to handle 'at least' and 'at most'.
teach.praise: Total minus the unwanted case — so quick! And for 'at most', add the allowed cases.
teach.nudge: Instead of adding many cases, what could you subtract from the total?

learn.hook: Make 5-letter words from DAUGHTER using 2 vowels and 3 consonants: first CHOOSE the letters, then ARRANGE them. Most hard problems are two easy ones glued together.
points: Mixed problems: number of ways = (ways to select) × (ways to arrange the selected objects).
Example: 2 vowels from 3 and 3 consonants from 5 in DAUGHTER, then arrange 5 letters: ³C₂ × ⁵C₃ × 5! = 3600.
Dictionary (rank) problems: list letters alphabetically; count words that begin with each smaller letter, then fix letters one by one.
Rows with restrictions: place the restricted group first (e.g. girls in even places), then the rest.
Always check whether letters are distinct; repeated letters need division by factorials.

example.q: If all arrangements of RANK are listed in dictionary order, what is the rank of RANK?
steps: Letters in order: A, K, N, R.
Words starting with A, K, N: 3 × 3! = 18.
Starting with R: next letter A; remaining K, N give RAKN (19th), RANK (20th).

learn.reallife: Password-strength meters estimate how many passwords an attacker must try — select characters, then arrange them.

games.title: Rank of MOTHER in dictionary order
items: Letters: E, H, M, O, R, T
MO then E, H or R: 3 × 3! = 18
MOT then E: 2! = 2; next MOTHER itself

items.q: Choose 3 of 5 people, seat in a row
2 vowels of 3 and 1 consonant of 4, arrange
Choose 2 of 5 books, arrange on shelf
Rank of CAT among arrangements of A, C, T

quiz.q: How many 5-letter words with 2 different vowels and 3 different consonants can be formed from the letters of DAUGHTER?
quiz.explain: Choose vowels ³C₂ = 3, consonants ⁵C₃ = 10, arrange 5 letters 5! = 120. 3 × 10 × 120 = 3600.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to arrange the chosen letters

quiz.q: The letters of LEMON are arranged in dictionary order. What is the rank of LEMON?
quiz.explain: Order: E, L, M, N, O. Starting with E: 24. L then E: LE + arrangements of M, N, O; LEMNO is 25th, LEMON is 26th.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to add 1 for the word itself

quiz.q: How many 4-letter words can be formed from 6 different letters if each word must have 2 specific letters? (Choose 2 more from the other 4, then arrange.)
In how many ways can 3 boys be chosen from 6 and seated in a row of 3 chairs?
Rank of the word ACT among all arrangements of A, C, T in dictionary order:
quiz.explain: ACT is the first word: A, then C, then T in alphabetical order.
quiz.mistake: Counts words before it instead of its position

quiz.q: How many 3-digit numbers with distinct digits can be formed by choosing 2 odd digits from 1, 3, 5 and 1 even digit from 2, 4?
quiz.mistake: Forgets one of the selection steps

quiz.q: In how many ways can 2 Physics and 2 Chemistry books be chosen from 4 Physics and 3 Chemistry books (all different) and placed on a shelf?
quiz.explain: ⁴C₂ × ³C₂ = 6 × 3 = 18 selections; each can be arranged in 4! = 24 ways. 18 × 24 = 432.

quiz.q: Why is the rank of a word found by counting words that come BEFORE it and adding 1?
options: Because every word is counted twice
Because its position is one more than the number of words ahead of it
Because the last letter is fixed
quiz.explain: If k words come earlier, the word is in position k + 1.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to add 1 for the word itself

teach.ask: Gappu must form words with 2 vowels and 3 consonants and then find a word's dictionary rank. Explain 'select then arrange' and how ranking works.
teach.praise: Pick first, then arrange — and count the words before mine for its rank. Chirpy clear!
teach.nudge: After choosing the letters, what is the next step?
